name: Arizona
sources: Rate 2.5%, 25% subtraction of net long-term gain on assets acquired after 2011, $2,100 exemption per person 65+: 2025 Form 140, https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/AZ/2025/FORMS_INDIVIDUAL_2025_140_f.pdf

2025 standard deduction ($15,750 single/MFS, $31,500 MFJ, $23,625 HOH) and use of federal Schedule A deductions: 2025 Form 140 booklet, https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/document/FORMS_INDIVIDUAL_2025_140Booklet.pdf

HB 4168 (2026): subtraction of the federal senior deduction (2025+), dependent credit $125 under 17 (2026+), $10,000 cap on itemized state and local taxes (2026+): https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57leg/2R/summary/H.HB4168_060926_APPROP.DOCX.htm

Dependent credit phaseout ($200,000; $400,000 joint) unchanged by HB 4168: https://www.currentfederaltaxdevelopments.com/blog/2026/6/14/arizona-hb-4168-title-43-income-tax-overhaul-aligned-with-the-one-big-beautiful-bill-act-obbba
provisional: 2026 standard deduction $15,750 / $31,500 / $23,625 per the legislature's HB 4168 summary (6/9/2026); enactment and any 2026 inflation indexing not confirmed
The $2,100 exemption for each person 65+ and the 25% long-term gain subtraction are from the 2025 Form 140.
Dependent credit phaseout (5% per $1,000 above $200,000, or $400,000 joint) is from a secondary summary of HB 4168.
The $5,000 itemized property-tax cap for married filing separately is assumed; the law states a $10,000 cap without a separate-filer figure.
notes: Assumes long-term gains are on assets bought after 2011, so 25% of them is subtracted.
